explanations.explanation: Bethsaida it is, friend. Luke says Jesus took the apostles away privately and withdrew to a town called Bethsaida (Luke 9:10). The apostles are the Twelve, the men Jesus sent out earlier. Just a quiet getaway with His closest followers, and you know how well quiet worked out.

Capernaum is a real town in the Gospels, so I see why it came to mind. But Luke 9:10 names a different place: Bethsaida. That's where Jesus withdrew with the apostles. The text gives us the town and nothing more, so I'll keep it simple too.

Nazareth is a famous town in the Gospels, but it isn't the one here. Luke says Jesus took the apostles away privately to a town called Bethsaida (Luke 9:10). I've mixed up my own cookie trays plenty of times, so no shame here. Bethsaida is the one to remember.

Not quite, friend. The text says the opposite: the crowds found out and followed Him, and He welcomed them (Luke 9:11). Nobody gets turned away at this door. I think that's worth a pause, because He had just gone away for some quiet and still opened His arms.

False is right! Luke 9:11 says that He welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God. No sending anybody away, no sign on the door. A crowd shows up uninvited and He makes room for them anyway.

Heals, yes! The text says He healed those who needed healing (Luke 9:11). So the crowd got teaching about the kingdom of God and healing, both in one afternoon. That's a full day of work before anybody even thinks about supper.

Anointing is a real thing in the Bible, but it's not what Luke 9:11 says here. The verse says Jesus healed those who needed healing. So the word that fits the blank is heals. Good guess on a Bible word, though, friend.

Baptizing shows up in the Bible, but not in this verse. Luke 9:11 says Jesus welcomed the crowds, spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and healed those who needed healing. So the blank wants heals. Easy one to mix up when so many Bible words are floating around.

explanations.answer: Send them off to find food and lodging
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker! The Twelve said, "Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding villages and countryside for lodging and provisions." (Luke 9:12) They also pointed out that they were in a desolate place. So their plan was to send everyone off to find a place to stay and something to eat.

explanations.answer: Have them share the food they brought
explanations.explanation: Nothing in the text says the crowd brought food to share. The Twelve asked Jesus to dismiss the crowd so they could find "lodging and provisions" in the villages and countryside (Luke 9:12). They gave the reason that they were in a desolate place. Sending people off was the request.

explanations.answer: Keep teaching them through the night
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say anything about teaching through the night. As the day neared its end, the Twelve asked Jesus to "Dismiss the crowd" so people could find lodging and provisions (Luke 9:12). Jesus had been teaching and healing all day, so I think that sounds like a long shift already.

Five loaves and two fish, right on the money. The disciples answered, "We have only five loaves of bread and two fish," (Luke 9:13). That's all they had, and they said it plainly. It's a small amount, and the text says it just like that.

explanations.answer: Seven loaves and a few fish
explanations.explanation: Close in spirit, but the numbers don't match. The disciples said, "We have only five loaves of bread and two fish," (Luke 9:13). Seven loaves shows up in a different story, so I see how it slipped in. For this one, hold on to five loaves and two fish.

You've got the right numbers in the wrong order, friend! It's five loaves and two fish, as the disciples said in Luke 9:13. I do that with my own recipes, and my cookies come out strange. Flip those numbers and you've got it.

explanations.answer: Sit down in groups of about fifty
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker! Jesus told His disciples, "Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each." (Luke 9:14) That was for about five thousand men. I'll leave the math to you, but that's a lot of little groups.

explanations.answer: Stand in lines of about a hundred
explanations.explanation: Nobody's standing in a line here. Jesus said, "Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each." (Luke 9:14) So it's sitting, and it's about fifty. A hundred is a nice round number, but it isn't the one in the verse.

explanations.answer: Walk to the nearest village together
explanations.explanation: That's what the Twelve suggested earlier, when they asked Jesus to dismiss the crowd so people could go to the villages (Luke 9:12). But Jesus gave a different instruction: "Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each." (Luke 9:14) So the crowd stays put and sits down.

True! Luke 9:15 says, "They did so, and everyone was seated." The disciples did what Jesus asked, and the whole crowd sat down. Getting thousands of people settled in groups is no small thing, friend.

Not false, friend. The text says, "They did so, and everyone was seated." (Luke 9:15) The disciples did exactly what Jesus told them, and the whole crowd sat down in groups. Everybody means everybody.
Heaven is right! Luke 9:16 says Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, spoke a blessing and broke them. He looked up before He broke the bread. That's the order the text gives.
The crowd was sitting right there, so it's a fair guess. But the text says Jesus looked up to heaven and spoke a blessing (Luke 9:16). The blank wants heaven. Then He broke the loaves and fish.

The disciples do have a part coming up, but not here. Luke 9:16 says Jesus looked up to heaven and spoke a blessing. After that, He gave the food to the disciples to set before the people. So heaven goes in the blank.

That one's false, friend. Luke 9:16 says Jesus broke the loaves and fish, and then "He gave them to the disciples to set before the people." So the disciples are the ones who set the food out. Jesus hands it over and they carry it to the crowd.

False is right! After He broke the loaves and fish, Jesus "gave them to the disciples to set before the people." (Luke 9:16) The disciples carried the food out to the crowd. They had been told to feed the people, and now they had food in their hands.
Satisfied, yes! Luke 9:17 says, "They all ate and were satisfied." Everyone ate, and everyone had enough. Five loaves and two fish, and nobody left hungry.
I bet it got pretty quiet while people ate, but the text doesn't say so. Luke 9:17 says, "They all ate and were satisfied." The blank wants satisfied. Everyone had enough to eat.
Nobody's restless in this verse, friend. Luke 9:17 says, "They all ate and were satisfied." Every person had enough. Restless fits an empty stomach, and these stomachs weren't empty anymore.

Twelve basketfuls, baker! Luke 9:17 says the disciples "picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over." After feeding about five thousand men, there was still food left to gather. I've never had that problem with a cookie tray.

Seven basketfuls shows up in a different feeding story, so it's an easy one to mix up. In this passage, the disciples "picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over." (Luke 9:17) Twelve is the number to hold on to here.

Three is a bit short, friend. Luke 9:17 says the disciples "picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over." Twelve full baskets, after everyone had eaten and been satisfied. That's a lot of leftovers.
